Reference counting and locking discipline for shared names and page table descriptors.
Concrete TLB flush primitives, page table lock acquisition, and cross CPU ordering guarantees.
Page and folio allocation, splitting, migration, and reclaim flows.
Interpretation of individual page flags, page types, and zone device private data.
Userfaultfd registration, fault delivery, and write protection handling beyond the flag test.

findings.text: One build variant provides an anonymous name lookup that always reports absence for any area.
The named container holds a reference count with a trailing variable length character sequence for the label.
One release helper drops the area associated name reference directly so it remains safe without requiring the address space lock.
Name equality holds on identical pointers; otherwise both handles must be present and their labels compare equal.
In the disabled configuration duplication and release are empty operations, name comparison always succeeds, and reference release does nothing.
Each address space carries a pending flush count starting at zero; contributors raise it before table updates and lower it after the corresponding range flush, while observers test for non zero.

Pending checks are meaningful only for the table lock already acquired; the increment is sequenced via table lock release and the decrement via flush completion, so a check observes pending state when its own table update is visible.
A nested flush query reports true only when more than one contributor is outstanding for the address space.
The flush count rests at zero, moves positive while updates are outstanding, and returns toward zero as flushes complete, with values above one indicating nesting.
Marker propagation during copy always retains error and guard indications and retains the write protect indication only when the destination area opts into write notifications.
Write notification membership is tested via an area flag mask in the enabled build and is always negative in the disabled build.
An area is considered to have recency unless it carries sequential or random read hints or its file is marked for no reuse.
A helper reports how many leading entries of a page pointer array form a physically adjacent run confined to one section.
The architecture vector size contribution is zero and the total vector size derives from arch plus base plus one doubled.
The types header defines its include guard macro.
Descriptor flags are wrapped in a single word record.
Page descriptor alignment is specified per build as either twice the word size or a single word size.

The base page descriptor starts with atomic flags and a multipurpose union covering cache or anonymous use with list, mapping, offset or share and private data, plus network pool, compound tail, device and RCU reuse, followed by a type or map count word, reference count and optional memory control, virtual address, CPU and sanitizer fields.

Bit zero of the first union word is reserved for tail detection and must not be reused; direct map tracking starts from negative one with defined transitions, private storage meaning depends on page state, and typed folio owners may borrow low type bits only while the type remains set.
Incorrect reuse of the shared union, direct manipulation of the reference count, or misuse of the optional virtual address on high memory systems risks corruption or stale mappings.
Pointer tagging reserves three low bits with designated positions for delayed reverse mapping and for a following page count encoding.
Helpers pack flags into low pointer bits or a shifted count and provide inverse extraction of flags, original pointer and count with validation of the flag range and count width.
Swap entries are single word values and soft leaf table entries share that representation.
A build marker selects whether large folios carry an explicit page count field.
Address space identity uses a signed count type with a matching maximum and an unsigned identifier type, narrow in one build and wide in another.

Identifier zero is reserved as dummy with the usable range starting after it; usable width is one less than the type width with derived mask and maximum, and folio encodings reserve distinct high bits for lock and shared state.

The folio header overlays the base page for its first slot and adds further slots for large mapping statistics and identity pairs, a deferred release list with 32 bit only counters, and huge page subpool, control, reservation and poisoning links.
Compile time checks require folio members to sit at the same offset as their page counterparts or at fixed one, two or three page strides for later slots.

Table descriptors carry flags, a reclaim or list or huge entry union, mapping storage, an index or owner or fragment count union with optional sharing count, a split or embedded table lock, type, reference count and optional memory control data.
Table members are required to match page offsets for shared storage.
A helper raises the shared table use count for huge page table sharing.
The maximum page structure shift is defined as the binary logarithm of the descriptor size.
Accessors expose the page private word for read and write and the folio private pointer for read, with area flags represented as an unsigned word.
Free pointers are wrapped as a single unsigned value.
A no MMU region node tracks tree linkage, flags, start, initialized end, allocated top, file offset, backing file, a usage count guarded by the region semaphore, and a flushed cache indicator.
Region usage counts must be accessed under the global no MMU region semaphore.
Fault handling context is either a single handler pointer with a null valued constant or an empty record with an empty constant, depending on build.
Area reference counting reserves bit thirty to exclude readers with a derived flag and a limit of one less than that flag.
NUMA balancing state per area records next scan time, active set reset time, two generations of approximate trapping process sets, and start and previous scan sequence numbers for eligibility.
PFN mapping tracking combines a reference count with a base frame number and a byte size.
Mapping completion is encoded with five tags distinguishing finished work from different remap and array mapping requests.

A mapping action carries a discriminated payload for remap ranges, simple I/O ranges or kernel page arrays, plus a type tag, an optional error override limited to valid codes, and a flag hiding the area from reverse mapping until setup completes.
Mapping setup starts with a requested action tag and ends in the complete state once the associated payload has been applied.
Area flags are stored as a fixed size bitmap sized by the machine word width with a defined empty value and an emptiness test.
The number of area flag bits equals the bits in a machine word.
An emptiness test reports whether no area flag bits are set.
An area descriptor separates fixed owner, file and range from updatable offset, file, flags and protections, plus single direction operations and private data and a follow up action.
Misuse of tagged pointers, incorrect count width, wrong folio slot access, invalid error overrides, or premature reverse map exposure can corrupt accounting or hide mappings.
External atomic increment used for flush and sharing counts.
External atomic read used for pending checks.
External atomic decrement used for flush completion.
External atomic initialization used for flush count reset.
External bitmap emptiness test used for flag checks.
External compile time assertion used for encoding validation.
